chapter.li: LEChapter1 Verse1 Paul and Silvanus and Timothy, the servants of God the Father and our Lord Jesus Christ, unto the church of the Thessalonians: VerseEnd Verse2 Grace unto you, and peace, from God our Father and the Lord Jesus Christ. VerseEnd

Verse3 We are bound to thank God always for you, brethren, as it is meet, because your faith grows exceedingly, and the charity of every one of you all toward each other abounds, VerseEnd Verse4 so that we ourselves glory in you in the churches of God, for your patience and faith in all your persecutions and tribulations that you endure VerseEnd — Verse5 which is a manifest token of the righteous judgment of God, that you may be counted worthy of the kingdom of God, for which you also suffer, VerseEnd Verse6 seeing it is a righteous thing with God to recompense tribulation to them that trouble you VerseEnd (Verse7 and to you who are troubled, rest with us) when the Lord Jesus shall be revealed from Heaven with his mighty angels VerseEnd Verse8 in flaming fire, taking vengeance on them that know not God and that obey not the gospel of our Lord Jesus Christ, VerseEnd Verse9 who shall be punished with destruction from the presence of the Lord, and from the glory of his everlasting power, VerseEnd Verse10 when he shall come to be glorified in his saints and to be awed in all them that believe (because our testimony among you was believed) in that day. VerseEnd

Verse11 Wherefore, also we pray always for you, that our God would count you worthy of this calling, and fulfill all the good pleasure of his goodness and the work of faith with power, VerseEnd Verse12 that the name of our Lord Jesus Christ may be glorified in you, and you in him, according to the grace of our God and the Lord Jesus Christ. VerseEnd

LEChapter2 Verse1 Now we implore you, brethren, by the coming of our Lord Jesus Christ and by our gathering together unto him, VerseEnd Verse2 that you be not soon shaken in mind, or be troubled by letter — except you receive it from us — neither by spirit or by word, as that the day of Christ is at hand. VerseEnd Verse3 Let no man deceive you by any means, for there shall come a falling away first, and that man of sin be revealed, the son of perdition VerseEnd Verse4 who opposes and exalts himself above all that is called God or that is worshipped, so that he, as God, sits in the temple of God, showing himself that he is God. VerseEnd Verse5 Do you not remember that when I was yet with you I told you these things? VerseEnd

Verse6 And now you know what withholds, that he might be revealed in his time; VerseEnd Verse7 for the mystery of iniquity does already work, and he it is who now works. And Christ suffers him to work until the time is fulfilled that he shall be taken out of the way. VerseEnd Verse8 And then shall that wicked one be revealed whom the Lord shall consume with the spirit of his mouth and shall destroy with the brightness of his coming; VerseEnd Verse9 yea, the Lord, even Jesus, whose coming is not until after there comes a falling away by the working of Satan with all power, and signs, and lying wonders, VerseEnd Verse10 and with all deception of unrighteousness, in them that perish because they received not the love of the truth that they might be saved. VerseEnd Verse11 And for this cause, God shall send them strong delusion, that they should believe a lie, VerseEnd Verse12 that they all might be damned who believed not the truth but had pleasure in unrighteousness. VerseEnd

Verse13 But we are bound to give thanks always to God for you brethren, beloved of the Lord, because God has from the beginning chosen you to salvation through sanctification of the spirit and belief of the truth, VerseEnd Verse14 unto which he called you by our gospel, to the obtaining of the glory of our Lord Jesus Christ. VerseEnd Verse15 Therefore, brethren, stand fast and hold the traditions which you have been taught, whether by word or our epistle. VerseEnd Verse16 Now our Lord Jesus Christ himself, and God, even our Father, who has loved us and has given us everlasting consolation and good hope through grace, VerseEnd Verse17 comfort your hearts and establish you in every good word and work. VerseEnd

LEChapter3 Verse1 Finally, brethren, pray for us, that the word of the Lord may have free course and be glorified, even as it is with you, VerseEnd Verse2 and that we may be delivered from unreasonable and wicked men; for all men have not faith. VerseEnd Verse3 But the Lord is faithful, who shall establish you and keep you from evil; VerseEnd Verse4 and we have confidence in the Lord concerning you, that you both do and will do the things which we command you. VerseEnd Verse5 And the Lord direct your hearts into the love of God and into the patient waiting for Christ. VerseEnd

Verse6 Now we command you, brethren, in the name of our Lord Jesus Christ, that you withdraw yourselves from every brother that walks disorderly and not after the tradition which he received of us, VerseEnd Verse7 for you know how you ought to imitate us; for we behaved not ourselves disorderly among you, VerseEnd Verse8 neither did we eat any man’s bread for naught, but wrought with labor and travail night and day that we might not be a burden to any of you VerseEnd — Verse9 not because we have not power, but to make ourselves an example unto you to imitate us. VerseEnd Verse10 For even when we were with you, this we commanded you: that if any would not work, neither should he eat; VerseEnd Verse11 for we hear that there are some who walk among you disorderly, working not at all, but are busybodies. VerseEnd

Verse12 Now them that are such, we command and exhort by our Lord Jesus Christ that with quietness they work and eat their own bread. VerseEnd Verse13 But you, brethren, be not weary in well-doing. VerseEnd Verse14 And if any man obey not our word by this epistle, note that man and have no company with him, that he may be ashamed; VerseEnd Verse15 yet count him not as an enemy, but admonish him as a brother. VerseEnd Verse16 Now the Lord of peace himself give you peace always, by all means. The Lord be with you all. VerseEnd
Verse17 The salutation of Paul with my own hand, which is the token in every epistle; so I write. VerseEnd Verse18 The grace of our Lord Jesus Christ be with you all. Amen. VerseEnd

p.i: The second epistle to the Thessalonians was written from Athens.
